status: DRAFT: prompts and assertions only; with-vs-without runs on Claude Code and Codex not done; schema to be checked against the NVIDIA skills guide

evals.prompt: I have an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://example.invalid/v1 serving my-model. Run a quick check of it on IFBench with NeMo Gym and tell me what I can report.
evals.expected_output: Installs or checks Gym (Python 3.13.14+), writes env.yaml or flags for the endpoint, runs gym eval prepare and a 5-task 1-repeat smoke, reads the metrics, and says the smoke score is not the benchmark score.
assertions: mentions Python 3.13.14 or newer and installing nemo-gym
runs or shows a smoke with --limit 5 and --num-repeats 1
states that a limited run's score is not the benchmark's score
does not put an API key in a committed file

evals.prompt: My Gym Slurm eval chain stopped after a TIMEOUT. The run id is gym-job-X, benchmark gpqa. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only gym eval resubmit <id> <benchmark> --recover --inspect, reads decision.action and gate_task.status, then runs the one action the decision table names; never plain gym eval resubmit.
assertions: starts with --recover --inspect and reads its output
does not use plain gym eval resubmit
names --max-walltime with --walltime-reason only when the cap is spent

evals.prompt: Run GPQA on my checkpoint on our Slurm cluster. I have the checkpoint path, account and partition. No Gym config exists yet.
evals.expected_output: Reads the model card, writes the vllm service and driver config with gym_install.ref pinned to a full commit, points the benchmark at benchmarks/gpqa config instead of copying it, validates with --resolve-only and --dry-run, smokes first.
assertions: pins gym_install.ref to a full 40-character commit
references the benchmark's own config instead of copying it
asks for or uses ${oc.env:...} placeholders for site values instead of inventing them

evals.prompt: I ran GPQA with limit 20 and got 62%. Can I put that in the report as the GPQA score?
evals.expected_output: No: a limit makes it a smoke; a benchmark score needs all tasks at no fewer than the benchmark's num_repeats, or a named versioned subset.
assertions: says the limited run is a smoke and not the benchmark score
names num_repeats from the benchmark manifest as the minimum

evals.prompt: Compare my BF16 run and the NVFP4 export on IFBench fairly in Gym.
evals.expected_output: Same config except model, served name and cache dtypes cited from the export's recipe; no --quantization flag; same Gym commit and num_repeats; resolve both and diff; pair tags in MLflow.
assertions: keeps the BF16 config except the fields quantization requires
uses the same Gym commit and num_repeats for both
resolves both configs and diffs them
